geometry_status: Archived 2-D convention. In Fig. 15 of doi:10.3970/cmes.2008.025.133 the 0.744 m dimension locates the box centre and H2 is 0.992 m from the downstream wall. In upstream coordinates the face is 2.3955 m and H2 is 2.228 m. For current 3-D runs see docs/marine_engineering_readiness.md.

reference.measured_quantity: water height in front of the obstacle, peak value and arrival time

geometry_provenance.reading: tank 3.22 x 1.00 m; column 1.228 x 0.550 m at the closed end; box 0.161 m (streamwise) x 0.161 m high, 0.403 m wide, upstream face at 1.228 + 1.248 = 2.476 m

Offshore Polar Eng. 30(4), doi:10.1142/s021987622050036x; open preprint arXiv:2306.01959, Fig. 2 (dimensioned setup reproduced from Kleefsman et al. 2005) and Sec. 'Computational domain and model parameters'.
verified_against: 3.22 m tank, 1.22 m column, 0.55 m column height, 0.40 x 0.16 x 0.16 m box placed 1.248 m downstream (A. English et al. 2021, doi:10.1007/s40571-021-00403-3, Sec. 'Three-dimensional dam-break flow with a fixed structure')

experimental_values.source: Kleefsman, Fekken, Veldman, Iwanowski & Buchner (2005) J. Comput. Phys. 206:363-393, doi:10.1016/j.jcp.2004.12.007, Fig. 19 right panel
experimental_values.source_pdf: https://pure.rug.nl/ws/files/2941055/2005JCompPhysKleefsman.pdf (research.rug.nl mirror is Cloudflare-gated; the pure.rug.nl mirror serves the same file)
experimental_values.digitisation: raster JPEG 1182x450 (page 22 image xref 314); x 0..6 s over px 661..1179, y 0.4..0.0 m over px 6.5..413.5

digitisation_cross_check.why: two curves traced independently by continuity; the paper states the impact instant is 'perfectly captured', so a digitisation that reproduces that agreement (<5 %) is self-consistent

uncertainty.reason: 1 px = 0.0038 m vertical, 0.0116 s horizontal; line thickness 3-6 px

experimental_values.previous_status_note: until this mission the field was WITHHELD because the paper PDF was believed unreachable; the pure.rug.nl mirror resolves that.
experimental_values.peak_time_derivation: peak_time_s is the argmax of the committed digitised H2 series (docs/m20884/outputs/kleefsman_h2_ref/h2_fig19.csv, 380 samples, t=0.3475..5.9653 s); the field was missing from this file until m21324, which blocked an event-window peak comparison even though the frozen protocol references the 1.703 s maximum. digitised_series is now a repo-root-relative path: the previous value "../../outputs/kleefsman_h2_ref/h2_fig19.csv" resolved to <repo>/outputs/, which does not exist.
experimental_values.arrival_time_definition: arrival_time_s = 0.3591 is the first DIGITISED SAMPLE whose level reaches the 0.02 m threshold; arrival_time_s_interpolated = 0.3481 is the linearly interpolated crossing of the same threshold, which is the operator the solver reports (tensorsph.kleefsman_obstacle._peak_metrics interpolates between the bracketing samples). The two readings of the same curve differ by 3.1 %, i.e. 0 % of the 10 % case tolerance. Both are scored (m21324) and a PASS must hold against both.

tolerance.rule: |got - ref| / |ref| < 0.10 for both the peak height and the arrival time

operators.height: legacy top-3 particle-centre mean (water_height_at); systematic bias -0.38..-1.33 dx
operators.surface: same with the (k-1)/2 dx row offset removed (surface_level); residual +/-0.5 dx
operators.slab: fixed physical aperture volume gauge (slab_level); dx-independent for a planar surface

metric_definition.why: the case-pool tolerance is 10 %, so the gauge itself must not carry a resolution-dependent bias of that size; measured on a still lattice, the historical operator is 1.8-2.7 cm low at dx=0.02 and 1.5-5.3 cm low at dx=0.04, i.e. it exceeds its own 0.02 m arrival threshold

frozen_primary.why: the audit of the committed bundle (docs/benchmarks/kleefsman-decidability-audit-m20773.md) measured a 9-20 % peak spread across the three water-level operators at the probe station, which is the same size as the 10 % case tolerance. The acceptance metric therefore cannot be evaluated until one operator is frozen: the fixed-aperture slab gauge is chosen because it is the only one of the three that is dx-independent for a planar surface, and the peak is taken after a 30 ms symmetric moving average because the particle-stack peak is set by ballistic spray (gauge-equivalent level, see convergence_analysis.py).

level-event vs front split (<=20 % of the deficit)

A uniform t_end=3.0 s dx0.01 run is submitted as cluster job cj3647; convergence_t30.py prefers results/gap_t30/ once it lands.

probe_station_lattice.what: is the committed 2.426 m station admissible for gauge H2?

evidence.probe_spacing_source: Amaro Junior, Cheng & Buruchenko (2020) Fig. 2a, three equal 0.496 m strings between the four wave probes
evidence.one_probe_in_reservoir: Kleefsman et al. (2005) p.381 (probes H1..H4); Fig. 19 caption p.383 names H4 as the reservoir probe
evidence.h2_location: Kleefsman et al. (2005) p.382: 'in the tank just in front of the box'
evidence.why_now: the committed provenance chain (geometry_provenance) reads only 1.228/1.248/0.744/0.161 and therefore never constrained the probe station: probe_offset = 0.05 m is a convention, not a measurement

committed_station.why: the committed station needs a = 1.434 m > column_length 1.228 m, i.e. H4 inside the tank, contradicting the primary source

anchor_gate.why: the only string that fixes H4 absolutely is the reservoir length: H4 sits at the reservoir/tank gate 1.228 m from the closed end

anchor_far_wall.why: the five figure strings must all dimension something; 1.150 m from the far (open) wall to H1 puts H1 at 2.070 m and H4 at 0.582 m, i.e. inside the reservoir

probe_station_lattice.verdict: COMMITTED_STATION_EXCLUDED; at the admissible gate anchor (2.220 m) arrival +7.8% (dx0.02) / +12.3% (dx0.04) and peak +8.4% (dx0.04, t=3 s) -- the case first reaches the tolerance band, but no PASS is issued until the full-horizon dx0.01 ladder lands (jobs cj4153 dx0.01/t3.0, cj4154 dx0.02/t3.0)
